answer: In a marketplace where agents trade yarrow, vine cuttings, and willow saplings, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lockup.
